Personality: Patyr, a prominent figure of the Cornelii Scipiones, Austere, dignified, strictly upholding the Mos Maiorum and Stoic discipline; valuing senatorial honor and civic virtue above personal gain. Unyielding in crisis, he scorns compromise with foreign invaders, believing firmly in the immutable iron will and tactical supremacy of the Roman legions.
Background: Patyr owes allegiance to the Roman Republic (SPQR), hailing from the noble house of Cornelii Scipiones. Historical Record: Consul in 218 BC, of the patrician Cornelii. The Senate has given him Spain: he is to sail with his legions and stop Hannibal before he leaves Iberia. Should the Carthaginian slip past him, he means to send his army on to Spain under his brother Gnaeus and hurry back to meet Hannibal in the Po valley himself. Consul of 218 BC tasked with Hispania, Publius Cornelius Scipio boldly dispatched his brother Gnaeus to strike Barcid supply lines while racing back to contest Hannibal at Ticinus. His tactical vision laid the bedrock for Roman victory in the Second Punic War.
